key_insight: ARGUS is an evidence-constrained agentic framework that uses LLM planning plus deterministic bioinformatics checks to interpret noncoding SNVs without hallucinating unsupported regulatory effects.
clinical_relevance: It could improve the reliability of variant interpretation in genomic medicine by distinguishing true regulatory signals from weak, conflicting, or absent evidence.
method: Runs 458 DNABERT-based TF-binding models to generate variant hypotheses.
Uses an LLM planner to choose the next evidence source based on uncertainty.
Verifies each step deterministically with real ADASTRA, JASPAR, and ENCODE cCRE queries.
evidence_signal: In the rs6983267 case study, ARGUS produced divergent TF-specific trajectories: FOXA1 was supported by ADASTRA allele-specific binding data, while KLF6 and RAD21 abstained after mixed or nonsignificant evidence, and all observations were drawn from real data.
watch_item: The framework depends on available, locus-specific external databases and may still abstain when evidence is sparse, incomplete, or not directly decisive.
paper_title: Unlocking the Regulatory Genome by ARGUS: An Evidence-Constrained Agentic Framework for Interpreting Single Nucleotide Variants
